comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C3, C27-C33, C93 regarding FMT efficacy in piglets. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the convergence of multiple experimental approaches with statistical significance, while peer reviewers describe findings as 'valuable' with 'solid' evidence and only 'minor weaknesses.'

Complete overlap on claims C4, C34-C39 regarding microbiome analysis and bacterial strain identification, but significant disagreement on evaluation. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED citing comprehensive analytical approaches, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to 'concerning ambiguity in methodology,' issues with 'rigor and reproducibility,' and advise 'readers should be cautious with interpretation.'

Strong overlap on claims C5, C40-C50 regarding mouse model findings on bacterial effects. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes comprehensive in vivo data with appropriate statistical tests, while peer reviewers acknowledge 'solid' evidence and praise 'multiple model systems.' Note: Peer R3 excludes C6-C7 which OpenEval R3 includes.

Partial overlap on claims C6-C7 (comparative efficacy between bacterial strains). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R3 includes these as part of broader mouse model findings, while peer R4 groups them with Wnt pathway mechanistic claims C51-C57.

Overlap on claims C51-C57 regarding Wnt pathway effects. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R4 covers broader set (C8, C51-C61) emphasizing pathway specificity and organoid corroboration, while peer R4 covers C6-C7, C51-C57 focusing on mechanistic investigations as a strength.

Overlap on claims C8, C58-C61 regarding proliferation markers and mechanistic findings. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R4 emphasizes multiple complementary approaches and pathway specificity, while peer R5 highlights 'valuable findings' and 'follow up mechanistic investigations' as strengths.

Overlap on claims C62-C64 regarding basal-out organoid experiments. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R5 covers broader organoid work (C9, C62-C71) with emphasis on Wnt inhibitor validation, while peer R6 focuses on limited basal-out effects with authors' explanation of restricted bacterial-epithelial interaction.

Strong overlap on claims C65-C71 regarding apical-out organoid findings. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes Wnt-dependent effects validated by inhibitor and differential results between organoid configurations, while peer reviewers praise 'multiple model systems' and 'mechanistic investigations' with Wnt-dependency validation.

Minimal overlap on claim C9 (organoid findings). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R5 includes C9 as part of comprehensive organoid experiments with Wnt inhibitor validation, while peer R5 groups C9 with main conclusions (C8, C10) and mechanistic investigations.

Overlap on claim C10 (main conclusions). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R6 focuses on integration of multi-model data (C10, C94) with mechanistic validation, while peer R5 groups C10 with organoid mechanistic data (C8-C10, C58-C61) as 'valuable findings' with 'solid evidence.'

OpenEval R7 addresses background and literature-based claims (C1-C2, C11-C26, C72-C87, C90-C92) rated as SUPPORTED based on appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval R8 addresses speculative explanations (C88-C89) rated as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these speculative claims.
